mechanisms.title: Credit Management
mechanisms.memory_hook: The order can be commercially correct and still not be releasable.
mechanisms.question: Is this exposure acceptable for this business partner and credit segment?
mechanisms.determination: The check rule executes one or more credit-check steps against the relevant partner/segment exposure and configured limits.
controls: delivery/billing progression depending on process configuration

failure_modes.prove: Check BP risk class/check rule → credit segment → limit/exposure → failed check step.
Verify the expected check rule and its assigned steps rather than only the credit limit.

tests.setup: Use a partner/segment with controlled limit and create one order below and one above the intended threshold.
tests.assert: Credit status follows the configured check rule and exposure.

mechanisms.title: Billing Relevance and Due Eligibility
mechanisms.memory_hook: Before asking how to invoice, prove what is allowed to become billable.
mechanisms.question: Which document is the billing basis, which quantity or status drives billing, and is the reference due now?

inputs.name: sales item category and billing relevance

mechanisms.determination: Item-category billing relevance defines whether billing is based on the sales document, delivery, billing plan, or another supported quantity/status basis. The billing due process then evaluates date, block, status, quantity and copying requirements before the reference is eligible for billing.

failure_modes.symptom: Expected reference is missing from the billing due list
failure_modes.prove: Trace item-category billing relevance → reference billing status → billing date/block → completeness → copying requirement.

failure_modes.symptom: Invoice quantity follows the wrong basis
failure_modes.prove: Separate billing relevance from billing quantity. Prove the item-category basis first, then the billing quantity rule in copying control.

tests.setup: Create one order-related and one delivery-related billable item with controlled item categories.
tests.assert: Each reference becomes due from the configured billing basis rather than from the document type alone.

tests.setup: Keep a billable reference valid but change only its billing block or due date.
tests.assert: The due-list eligibility changes without changing the underlying billing relevance.

mechanisms.title: Billing Plan Determination and Date Control
mechanisms.memory_hook: A billing plan moves the commercial clock into the sales item.
mechanisms.question: Does this item require a billing plan, which plan type applies, and which plan date is currently billable?

inputs.name: amount, percentage and date-level billing block

mechanisms.determination: The item category can require a billing plan and select its configured type. The plan type and date rules build periodic or milestone billing dates. Each date carries its own due context, amount or percentage, status and optional billing block.
configuration_surfaces: Assign billing plan type through item-category control
Billing plan date proposal and horizon

failure_modes.symptom: Order item has no expected billing plan
failure_modes.prove: Check item category → billing-plan requirement/type → relevant sales-document context before editing dates manually.

failure_modes.symptom: Milestone or periodic date is not billable
failure_modes.prove: Check generated plan date → billing block/status → milestone confirmation or periodic date context → due eligibility.

failure_modes.symptom: Wrong amount is due on one plan date
failure_modes.prove: Separate item pricing from date-level percentage/amount in the billing plan and prove which value owns the due amount.

tests.setup: Use one periodic and one milestone-controlled item in controlled configuration.
tests.assert: The correct billing plan type and schedule are proposed from item/process control.

tests.setup: Set a billing block on one plan date while leaving another date open.
tests.assert: Only the blocked plan date is prevented from billing.

mechanisms.title: Billing Type Determination
mechanisms.memory_hook: Billing relevance says what can be billed. Billing type says what kind of billing document will be created.
mechanisms.question: Which billing document type is proposed for this reference and business transaction?

inputs.name: configured billing type for the reference process
target billing type in copying control
manual/default billing type override where allowed

mechanisms.determination: The reference document and configured billing relationship propose the target billing document type. Copying control must support the source/target combination. In supported billing-due processing, a user or scheduled process can provide a different billing type for a specific business need such as a pro forma invoice.

failure_modes.prove: Trace reference document type → configured billing type → source/target copying control → any due-list override.

failure_modes.symptom: Desired billing type cannot be created from the reference
failure_modes.prove: Check whether the source/target billing relationship and copying-control combination exists before changing document data.

tests.setup: Create two supported reference processes that are configured for different target billing types.
tests.assert: Each reference proposes the expected target billing type.

tests.setup: Use a supported due-list override for a controlled billing scenario.
tests.assert: The override changes the target billing type without changing the source reference document.

mechanisms.title: Billing Split and Convergence
mechanisms.memory_hook: A billing split is usually a header-consistency problem wearing an invoice costume.
mechanisms.question: Can these billable items share one billing-document header, or must SAP create separate documents?

inputs.name: billing type and default billing date

mechanisms.determination: During billing, the system groups eligible items when the values that must become common billing-header data are compatible. Differing split-relevant values force separate billing documents. Copying-control choices, individual-billing settings, and custom data-transfer logic can also force or prevent selected split situations where the standard fields allow it.
configuration_surfaces: Reference/assignment number transfer in copying control
Custom Data Transfer for Billing Documents

failure_modes.symptom: Two deliveries create two invoices instead of one
failure_modes.prove: Run split analysis and compare billing type/date, partner, organizational, currency, payment, Incoterms and reference/assignment-number fields before changing routines.

failure_modes.symptom: One reference document creates several billing documents
failure_modes.prove: Compare item-level values that are promoted to billing-header fields; a single reference does not guarantee a single billing document.

failure_modes.symptom: Business wants one invoice but standard fields force a split
failure_modes.prove: Classify the differing field first. Some standard split fields cannot simply be cleared; only selected fields can be normalized through supported data-transfer logic.

tests.setup: Bill two compatible references, then change one standard split-relevant field on one reference.
tests.assert: Compatible items converge; the changed field forces a separate billing document and split analysis identifies it.

tests.setup: Bill a single reference whose items carry two different values that become billing-header data.
tests.assert: The system creates multiple billing documents when the item differences require different billing headers.

mechanisms.title: Billing Lifecycle Orchestration
mechanisms.memory_hook: VF04 is a worklist. Billing is a chain of eligibility, target, transfer, grouping and posting decisions.
mechanisms.question: How does an eligible sales or delivery reference become the final billing document and downstream financial event?

inputs.name: copying control, quantity and pricing transfer

mechanisms.determination: Billing orchestrates the specialized controls: prove that the reference is due, determine the target billing type, apply copying control and pricing/quantity transfer, group compatible items into billing documents, then create and post the billing result according to billing-type and financial controls.

failure_modes.symptom: Billing fails or produces an unexpected result
failure_modes.prove: Do not debug Billing as one block. Classify the symptom into BILLREL → BILLPLAN if relevant → BILLTYPE → COPY/pricing → BILLSPLIT → posting/output.

failure_modes.symptom: Billing document exists but financial or output result is wrong
failure_modes.prove: Separate successful billing creation from downstream account determination, FI transfer and output processing.

tests.setup: Run a controlled order-related and delivery-related scenario through eligibility, target billing type, copying control and grouping.
tests.assert: The billing document reflects the outputs of the specialized billing controls and creates the expected downstream status.
